# Tomer Yona

> Personal site of Tomer Yona, PhD: wearable sensor measurement, validation and evidence generation. Also home to free tools he made, including Cuewand, a phone remote for PowerPoint.

## Cuewand: free phone remote for PowerPoint

Cuewand turns a phone into a remote control for Microsoft PowerPoint on a Windows laptop. The phone needs no app: it scans a QR code shown on the laptop (or opens a short address and types a 6-digit number) and the remote opens as a web page in the phone's browser. It is built for iPhone and Android browsers.

What the phone does:
- Next and Back (slide clicker / presentation clicker / wireless presenter replacement)
- Speaker notes on the phone, split at each animation step when the notes contain [click]; pictures of the current and next slide
- A countdown for the talk on the Next button, with on-screen alerts; on Android it also vibrates (iPhones do not let web pages vibrate). The clock starts when the slide show starts or with the first Next, as chosen; for a lesson it can be turned off ("No clock")
- Laser pointer: holding the slide picture moves PowerPoint's red laser dot on the big screen
- Zoom on the big screen (a trial in 2.6): + and - on the phone zoom PowerPoint's slide show; zoomed in, dragging the picture moves around the slide
- Find a slide by title, slide text, notes or number and jump to it; after a jump to a hidden backup slide, Back returns to where you were
- Black out the screen
- Rehearsal timing, then "ahead / behind" pacing during the talk
- Any number of phones; by default every one can press Next, and control can be passed to one co-presenter while the others follow
- Works alongside a hardware clicker or the keyboard
- Tablet presenter view in landscape; left-handed layout

Requirements and limits:
- 64-bit Windows laptop with the PowerPoint desktop app, run on the computer that shows the slides and set up before the talk (not meant for an unfamiliar lectern PC). No Mac version; Keynote and PowerPoint on the web are not supported. The Windows download bundles its own Python, and every program file in it is signed, so Windows Smart App Control lets it run.
- Phone and laptop connect over the same Wi-Fi, the phone's own hotspot, or an optional internet link relayed encrypted through Cloudflare quick tunnels. Same Wi-Fi traffic is not encrypted.
- Without a PowerPoint deck open, Next and Back press the laptop's arrow keys, which works for Google Slides or a full-screen PDF (no notes, slide pictures or pace; the clock still runs).
- Anyone with the pairing code or 6-digit number can control the slides while Cuewand runs; codes last twelve hours, and Make new codes on the pairing page cancels them sooner.

Testing status (version 2.6): version 2.1 passed a full self-test on real PowerPoint 16 on Windows 11, and version 2.6 ran there with presses, slide pictures and notes from a real phone (one presenter). Every change is checked against a PowerPoint simulator with 683 automated checks and an automated accessibility audit. The real phone was an Android phone with Chrome. Not yet tried: any iPhone, vibration on a real phone, the hotspot route, the internet link since a reported failure, [click] notes and sections on a real deck, PowerPoint Presenter View with two screens, and a real screen reader. The full self-test has not been rerun on real PowerPoint since version 2.1, and zoom on the big screen is a trial.

Price and licence: free, open source (MIT). No accounts, ads, analytics or tracking; nothing is sent to the author.

- [Cuewand page, with a live interactive demo](https://www.tomeryona.com/cuewand/)
- [Source code and full manual on GitHub](https://github.com/TomerIL/cuewand)
- [Download for Windows (Cuewand-for-Windows.zip)](https://github.com/TomerIL/cuewand/releases/latest)

## The Jefferson curl, measured

The Jefferson curl is a loaded spinal flexion exercise: a standing lifter holds a weight and flexes the spine sequentially from the neck downward, lowering the weight toward the feet.

The page shows one lifter performing the Jefferson curl and the Romanian deadlift (RDL) side by side with the same 45 kg, as an interactive film reconstructed from motion capture (41 markers) and surface EMG (10 sensors), with three stills: standing, halfway down and the bottom. At the bottom of the lift this lifter's spine was flexed 38 degrees in the Jefferson curl and 10 degrees in the Romanian deadlift; the hips 109 and 122 degrees; the knees 2 and 32 degrees.

What the study found (the first surface EMG characterization of the Jefferson curl; 21 resistance-trained adults; the same absolute load in both lifts, mean 41.9 kg, set in the Jefferson curl at a Borg rating of perceived exertion of 16). Muscle activity, as a percentage of maximal voluntary isometric contraction, Jefferson curl vs Romanian deadlift:
- Upper erector spinae: 63 vs 45 (higher in the Jefferson curl)
- Lower erector spinae: 60 vs 48 (higher in the Jefferson curl)
- Biceps femoris: 54 vs 42 (higher in the Jefferson curl)
- Middle erector spinae: 52 vs 56 (no significant difference)
- Gluteus maximus: 31 vs 31 (no significant difference)

Not measured: load on the spine, injury risk, flexibility, training outcomes. The study supports no claim about safety.

- [The Jefferson curl, measured](https://www.tomeryona.com/jefferson-curl/)
- [The paper, open access](https://doi.org/10.26603/001c.172559): Yona T, Kalifa B, Gildar S, Margi R, Har-Nir I, Fischer AG. Surface EMG Characterization of the Jefferson Curl at a Submaximal Load Matched to the Romanian Deadlift: A Cross-Sectional Study in Resistance-Trained Adults. International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy. 2026;21(11):1100-1116.

## Other tools

- [MVNX Viewer](https://www.tomeryona.com/mvnx-viewer/): free browser-based viewer for .mvnx motion-capture files (Movella / Xsens MVN export): 3D skeleton playback, joint-angle charts, foot contacts, centre of mass. Files are not uploaded.

- [Jiu-jitsu biomechanics in 3D](https://www.tomeryona.com/jiu-jitsu-biomechanics/): two grappling positions (an arm bar and an Americana) reconstructed in 3D from single photos with computer vision. SAM 3 separates the two people, MoGe-2 estimates the camera and the mat, and SAM 3D Body estimates each person's 3D joint centres and body mesh; eight joint angles per person are computed from the joint centres, and an anatomical skeleton (BodyParts3D) is posed inside each body. Interactive 3D view in the browser. The values are estimates from one image.

## Open data

- [COMPWALK-ACL dataset on Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15624356): multi-pace IMU gait kinematics (Xsens Awinda) from 92 participants: healthy adults, healthy adolescents, and people with an ACL injury before and three months after reconstruction. CC BY 4.0. Trials are .mvnx files with paired .xlsx spreadsheets.
- [The COMPWALK-ACL paper, Scientific Data (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-06307-8): Yona T, Peskin B, Fischer A.

## About

- [Home](https://www.tomeryona.com/): postdoctoral researcher at Maastricht University; PhD in Biomedical Engineering (Technion); licensed physiotherapist. Work spans IMU, EMG, PPG and accelerometry, from single-patient assessments to 10,000-participant cohorts.
